videos.script: A tool that has to be recompiled to change a setting is a tool nobody uses twice. This lesson gives yours a command line. {{define}} You declare each flag with a name, a default and a line of help. Then one call to Parse fills them all, typed. A duration flag reads one second as a duration. {{help}} The help text is written for you. Ask for it and the program exits cleanly. Give a flag the wrong kind of value and it refuses, with status two. {{traps}} Two traps fail in silence. A word before the flags stops the parsing early. And a true or false flag needs an equals sign. {{custom}} Then flags of your own type: one you can repeat, a number that must be a port, an address checked by the type that owns it. {{sub}} Last, subcommands, the shape of the go command itself. Each one gets its own set of flags. {{close}} Lesson 22 is about what a program says while it runs: structured logs.
